It is. Red, blue and yellow are prime colors. Green, purple, orange and secondary ones. Don't know why green is replacing yellow in this vid as a prime.
It is the way how your neurons work, he demonstrates it in a great way with 3 colored lights.

Human eyes only see Red, Green and Blue. (Hence why TVs use RGB technology, consisting only of Red (R), Green (G) and Blue (B) colors dots.)

Then, once the cones pass on the brightness of these three wavelengths, the 2 receptor types then filter out the Blue on one side, and Green on the other. If the intensity of R + G > B, you see Yellow. If the intensity of the R + G < B, you see Blue. The other receptor filters out the Blue, so if R+B > G, you see red. If R+B < G, you see Green.

The mixing of colors in paint isn't actually how the eye works, it is taking a + B and a -B, and mixing it together, canceling out the B, as in +1B - 1B = 0B. This leaves us with G, as the R is small. To get Orange is the same process, but the R > the G.
